text: Ghulam Nabi Azad, born on 7 March 1949, in Soti, Gandoh tehsil (Bhalessa), Doda district of the erstwhile princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, is an Indian politician who served as Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha from 2014 to 2021. He was the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir from 2005 to 2008 and served as Minister of Health and Family Welfare. Azad held the position of Minister of Parliamentary Affairs in the Manmohan Singh government until 27 October 2005, when he became Chief Minister. He also served as Deputy Minister in charge of Law, Justice and Company Affairs in 1982 after being elected to the Seventh Lok Sabha from Washim, Maharashtra. He was a member of the Rajya Sabha from Maharashtra between 1990 and 1996 and later represented Jammu and Kashmir in the Rajya Sabha from 30 November 1996 to 29 November 2002 and again from 30 November 2002 to 29 November 2008, resigning on 29 April 2006 upon becoming Chief Minister. He was elected to the Eighth Lok Sabha in 1984. During the Rao government, he held portfolios of Parliamentary Affairs and Civil Aviation. His government in Jammu and Kashmir collapsed in July 2008 when the People's Democratic Party withdrew support, leading Azad to resign on 7 July 2008 and leave office on 11 July 2008. In the second United Progressive Alliance Government, he served as Health Minister, where he promoted the National Rural Health Mission and launched the National Urban Health Mission for slum dwellers. He advocated a late marriage age of 25 to 30 for population control and linked rural childbearing to lack of electricity and TV entertainment. In June 2014, he was appointed Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha after the National Democratic Alliance formed the Union government. In 2015, he was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jammu and Kashmir despite the PDP-BJP alliance holding a majority in the Legislative Assembly. On 26 August 2022, Azad resigned from all positions, including primary membership of the Indian National Congress, citing the destruction of the consultative process by Rahul Gandhi. Sonia Gandhi accepted his resignation. On 4 September 2022, he announced the formation of a new political party, stating that the people of Jammu and Kashmir would decide its name and flag. On 26 September 2022, he officially announced the name of the new party as the Democratic Progressive Azad Party, which has a flag with three colours: mustard, white, and blue. Azad is the chief patron and founder of the Democratic Progressive Azad Party. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for public affairs. In September 2023, he was a member of a government committee to suggest constitutional changes for simultaneous polls. He married Shameema Dev Azad, a well-known Kashmiri singer, in 1980, and they have a son, Saddam Nabi Azad, and a daughter, Sofiya Nabi Azad. He completed his Bachelor's of Science at G.G.M. Science College, Jammu, and earned a Master's in Zoology from the University of Kashmir, Srinagar, in 1972. He began his political career as secretary of the Block Congress Committee in Bhalessa in 1973, was elected President of the Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Youth Congress in 1975, and later became President of the All-India Youth Congress in 1980.
